title: Shiblon Receives the Sacred Things
summary: In the thirty-sixth year, Shiblon takes possession of the sacred things delivered to Helaman. Shiblon and his brother are described as upright and obedient.

explicit_facts.text: In the commencement of the thirty-sixth year, Shiblon took possession of sacred things delivered to Helaman by Alma.
Shiblon was just and walked uprightly before God, continually doing good and keeping God's commandments; his brother did also.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and contents of the sacred things.
The appearance and identity of Shiblon's brother.

narration.text: Shiblon took possession of those sacred things

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Helaman or Alma as present; the verse reports a transfer to Shiblon without stating they are there.

title: Moroni Dies

title: Corianton’s Voyage and Shiblon’s Death
summary: In the thirty-ninth year of the reign of the judges, Shiblon died. Corianton had gone by ship to the land northward to carry provisions to the people who had gone there.

explicit_facts.text: Shiblon died in the thirty-ninth year of the reign of the judges.
Corianton had gone to the land northward in a ship to carry provisions to people who had gone there.

narration.text: Shiblon died also, and Corianton had gone forth to the land northward in a ship, to carry forth provisions unto the people who had gone forth into that land.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Shiblon aboard the ship or depict his death occurring during Corianton’s voyage.

title: Record of the Sacred Things Conferred Upon Helaman
summary: The sacred things had been conferred upon Helaman, son of Helaman, before Shiblon's death.

explicit_facts.text: It became expedient for Shiblon to confer the sacred things before his death upon Helaman, son of Helaman, who was named after his father.
The sacred things were to be kept sacred and handed down from one generation to another.
In this year, the sacred things had been conferred upon Helaman before Shiblon's death.

unspecified_visual_details: The source does not specify the appearance or contents of the sacred things, the location, or the manner of conferral.
Typography and a neutral background for a text-only presentation are creative design choices.

narration.text: Nevertheless, these things were to be kept sacred, and handed down from one generation to another; therefore, in this year, they had been conferred upon Helaman, before the death of Shiblon.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Use a text-only presentation of the reported event, not a staged transfer or flashback.
Shiblon and Helaman are mentioned in the account, not established as visibly present in a narrated scene.
Helaman's father is identified only through the stated relationship and naming.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Shiblon and Helaman together or depict a physical handover.
